Mali.title: Defence and security: The Transitional President holds discussions with the military command
Mali.summary: On Tuesday, 24 November 2020, in Koulouba, the Transitional President, Head of State and Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi Goïta, chaired a meeting with the Chiefs of Staff and the Directors of Services of the Defence and Security Forces. The aim of this meeting was to assess the situation of the forces, strengthen the coherence of the command structure, and define the strategic and operational priorities of national defence.

Mali.title: San: Police station attacked by armed men
Mali.summary: Armed men attacked the police station in San on the afternoon of Tuesday, 24 November 2020, according to local sources. The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) responded. According to the same sources, the gunfire has ceased and the situation is now under the control of the FAMa.

Mali.source: Timbuktu Institute (African Center for Peace Studies)
Mali.title: Jihadism in the Sahel: “The states of the region cannot remain in this situation of neither war nor peace forever”
Mali.summary: Should we negotiate with the jihadists in the Sahel? With the ongoing conflict between the juntas of the Alliance of Sahel States (AES) and the al-Qaeda-linked terrorist group JNIM, the question is becoming less and less taboo, especially as the military solutions that have been in vogue for over a decade are not working. In a report published on Friday, 20 November, experts from the International Crisis Group (ICG) therefore recommend that the authorities in Bamako, Ouagadougou and Niamey open frank negotiations with him.

Mali.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: 34 terrorists neutralised and more than 90 motorbikes destroyed in four days
Mali.summary: Between 20 and 23 November 2026, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, carried out a series of strikes against the logistics of terrorist groups, as part of Operation Dougoukoloko. . Report announced by the Armed Forces General Staff: 34 terrorists neutralised, one ammunition depot, one gold processing site, three pick-up trucks and more than 90 motorbikes destroyed.

Mali.title: Koulouba: The Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces convenes the military hierarchy to assess the security situation
Mali.summary: DEFENCE AND SECURITY: The Transitional President holds discussions with the military command The Transitional President, Head of State and Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, His Excellency Army General Assimi Goïta, chaired a meeting with the Chiefs of Staff and the Directors of Services of the Defence and Security Forces on Tuesday, 24 November 2020 at Koulouba.

Mali.title: MDAC: The 24 soldiers released following an air-land operation were received by the Minister Delegate
Mali.summary: Following their release on Wednesday, 18 November 2026, in the In-Tebezas area near Kidal, the 24 soldiers who had previously been held hostage were received on Monday, 23 November 2026, by the Minister Delegate to the Minister of Defence and Veterans' Affairs, Major General Oumar Diarra. The meeting, which took place in the department's conference room, was attended by the Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces (CEMGA), Major General Élysée Jean DAO.

Mali.title: Defence and security: The Transitional President holds discussions with the military command
Mali.summary: The Transitional President, Head of State and Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, His Excellency General of the Army Assimi Goïta, chaired a meeting with the Chiefs of Staff and the Directors of Services of the Defence and Security Forces on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, in Koulouba. . The aim of this meeting was to assess the situation of the forces, strengthen the coherence of the command structure, and define the strategic and operational priorities of national defence.

Mali.title: Koulouba: Assimi Goïta convenes military leaders to set defence priorities
Mali.summary: The Transitional President, Army General Assimi Goïta, met with the Chiefs of Staff and the Directors of Services of the Defence and Security Forces on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, in Koulouba. On the agenda: the state of the armed forces, the organisation of the command structure and national defence priorities . Discussions focused on the situation of the FAMa, the strengthening of their resources, and the adaptation of their organisation to the fight against insecurity.

Mali.title: Ségou: Three suspects arrested in connection with the murder of a young man in Markala
Mali.summary: Three suspects were arrested on Thursday 19 November 2026 as part of the investigation into the murder of a young man, which took place on 12 November in Markala, 35 km from Ségou. The victim had been killed on a construction site belonging to his brother. According to local sources, the suspects are being held at the gendarmerie.

Mali.title: Mali: Algerian secret services reportedly seeking to resume mediation with the FLA, according to Africa Intelligence
Mali.summary: The Algerian secret services are reportedly seeking to re-establish a channel of dialogue between the Malian authorities and the National Movement for the Liberation of Azawad (MNLA), according to Africa Intelligence. "As a new offensive by armed groups looms, the Algerian secret services are struggling to reactivate channels of mediation between the Malian state and the Tuareg rebels allied with the jihadists of GSIM," wrote the specialised media outlet on X, on 24 November 2026.

Mali.title: "Don't leave, stay in the country": Racky Aidara becomes a victim of cyberbullying after her advice
Mali.summary: "Don't leave, stay in the country": Racky Aidara victim of cyberharassment after her advice Given the deaths in clandestine emigration in recent weeks, all Senegalese opinion leaders are talking about it and advising young people who are thinking of doing so. As the tragedies of clandestine emigration have multiplied in recent weeks, there are an increasing number of Senegalese voices calling on young people to give up on leaving.

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: China-Solomon Islands: Beijing defends its cooperation in the Pacific
Mali.summary: Bamako, 24 November (AMAP) China stated on Tuesday that its cooperation with Pacific island countries is not aimed at geopolitical competition or confrontation between blocs, amid reports of a possible non-renewal of its security agreement with the Solomon Islands. "China is developing its relations with the Solomon Islands on the basis of mutual respect and equality," said Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun at a press briefing in Beijing.

Mali.title: The Minister Delegate for Defence welcomes servicemen released from captivity
Mali.summary: The Minister Delegate for Defence welcomes soldiers released from captivity General Oumar Diarra, Minister Delegate to the Minister of Defence, welcomed Malian soldiers recently released from captivity on 23 November 2026. These soldiers had been captured during the coordinated attacks of 25 April 2026, particularly in the Kidal region. According to Major General Elizée Jean Dao, Chief of Staff of the Army, their release is the result of a major operation carried out by the command.

Mali.title: Soldiers freed in Mali: spectacular raid by the FAMA and Africa Corps, or an operation carried out without fighting?
Mali.summary: Soldiers freed in Mali: spectacular raid by the FAMa and Africa Corps, or operation carried out without a fight? On 18 November, the Malian army and its Russian partners announced that they had freed 24 soldiers being held near Kidal. But behind the spectacular images released by Africa Corps, the reality of the operation is said to be less heroic.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: Mobile money scams cost over CFAF 104 million (October)
Burkina Faso.summary: Mobile money scams have become widespread in Burkina Faso. According to data provided by the Ministry of Security, Mobile Money scams claimed 263 victims in October, resulting in financial losses of around CFAF 104 million. These figures highlight the impact of digital fraud on the losses suffered by the population.

Niger.title: Abolish pipeline surveillance contracts
Niger.summary: There is something insanely absurd in having to incentivise any group of persons to restrain them from destroying assets in which they have significant stakes. This is even more so when the environmental costs of such destruction are considered. That absurdity writ large in Nigeria at the dawn of the Fourth Republic, under the term “Pipelines surveillance contracts”.

Niger.title: Urban security: around thirty unlicensed taxis seized during an inspection operation in Niamey
Niger.summary: As part of its efforts to regulate and make urban transport safer, the Urban Transport Department of the City of Niamey (DTU) carried out an operation this weekend to check and sweep for vehicles operating without regulatory authorisation, particularly in markets and busy areas of the capital. The operation, which covered several neighbourhoods and junctions in the capital, resulted in the seizure of vehicles used for the illegal transport of people, including around thirty unlicensed taxis.
